Subject: Post-call: p95/p99 end-to-end latency qualification & POC kickoff (HelixHealth)

Hi Michael / Jessie —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary objective: validate end-to-end p95 / p99 latency targets for your assistant flows comparing your current provider vs Redwood hosted API.
- Example targets you mentioned: p95 in the ~200–300ms ballpark, p99 < ~500ms (end-to-end, including client/network overhead).
- Traffic shape: daily steady traffic with morning peak; peak concurrency reported ~120–150; ~80% of requests use streaming to deliver assistant tokens.
- Payloads: mixture of short single-turn prompts (avg ~40 tokens) and longer contextful requests (avg ~320 tokens).

Proposed POC scope (Redwood-run, head-to-head)
1) Exchange artifacts: traffic profile CSV, sample payloads, and either current-provider logs or a replay/sandbox endpoint (we can work with logs if you prefer).
2) Test scenarios: steady-state baseline (60 qps sustained, concurrency target ~120) and burst tests (200 qps bursts for 5 minutes). Streaming measurement includes time-to-first-token (TTF) and time-to-last-token (TTL).
3) Acceptance criteria (draft):
   - End-to-end p95 <= 250ms (sustained for 90% of 1-hour windows during the test run)
   - End-to-end p99 <= 450ms
   - Streaming: p95 TTF < 120ms, and consistently lower average TTL vs current provider for similar token counts

We can refine the acceptance numbers based on what you share from current-provider baseline metrics.

Next steps / asks from Helix
- Please send the traffic_profile.csv and sample_payloads.jsonl (redacted is fine).
- If possible, provide current-provider end-to-end logs or a replay token/sandbox endpoint so we can run an apples-to-apples replay.
- Confirm the typical peak concurrency and any rate limits we should be aware of.

Proposed timeline
- Share artifacts by EOD 10/05
- Redwood runs test window (48 hours of combined scenarios) starting 10/06–10/07
- Results and recap meeting the week of 10/12

Ben will lead the test execution; Laura will observe and validate metrics. I’ll coordinate the kickoff meeting once we have the artifacts.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

Best,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwoodinference.com

Thanks Michael — useful numbers. Quick technical follow-up and a proposed test plan outline so Helix can confirm: 

Proposed test scenarios (we'll provide a more detailed test-plan.pdf):
1) Baseline steady-state replay: replay a 3-hour slice at your observed steady qps (we'll start at 60 qps) to measure sustained p95/p99 and resource behavior.
2) Peak replay: replay the morning ramp (shape included in traffic_profile.csv) with concurrency up to 150 and short spikes to 200 for stress checks.
3) Streaming-focused: replay only streaming calls and measure both time-to-first-token (TTF) and time-to-last-token (TTL).

Measurement and instrumentation
- We'll add X-Redwood-Trace headers to each request for trace correlation. Please confirm your observability team is fine with correlating traces to the S3 logs we pull.
- For streaming TTF we will measure server->client first byte latency; for TTL we will compare total end-to-end generation time for identical token counts.

Questions / asks
- Can Helix provide a short-lived sandbox API key for the current-provider endpoint, or would you prefer us to run the replay against a recorded log set? The former lets us do live head-to-head tests; the latter is perfectly fine for apples-to-apples comparisons if you prefer to avoid live calls.
- We'll produce a draft test-plan.pdf (attached) showing exact ramp schedules and sample curl commands; please review and comment.

If the above looks good I’ll schedule the execution and share expected cost estimate for the Redwood-hosted run (token & throughput billing estimate).

—Ben
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: test-plan.pdf (pdf)
